opening.headline: If there is no improvement despite continuing to revise the guidelines, the type of failure must be judged by pairing it with the area to be fixed among the guidelines, knowledge, and connector.
body: If you answered the wrong price and corrected the instructions 10 times, but the error remains the same and the instructions only become more complicated, you did not select the correct location according to the symptom. Assistants aren't just about instructions. The knowledge you reference and the connectors you bring also determine the outcome.

In this lesson, we will distinguish between the three components that make up the assistant and see which component corresponds to which type of failure. Next, we look at how to recheck after revision and the risks of excessive revision, and explain a case where a pricing error was a data update issue rather than a guideline.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can describe failure types and component responses
You can distinguish between instructions, knowledge, and connectors for modification.
You can evaluate whether the corrective judgment is reasonable.

screens.title: I keep revising the guidelines, but there is no improvement.
screens.lead: First, read the story of a team that changed its instructions ten times.

visual.alt: The instruction document is getting longer and longer, but the price error speech bubble remains the same.
labels: The price is exactly the same

paragraphs: One team's assistant responded with the past price of the product. The team added the phrase ‘prices will be accurately provided’ in the guidelines, but it was of no use. I revised it ten times by changing sentences, making it longer, and adding examples.
As the instructions got longer, the other answers that had nothing to do with price started to get weirder. The error remains the same, but the instructions have become more complicated.

This happens because you don't choose the right place for the symptoms. If the reason the assistant answered the old price is in the instructions, it is correct to change the instructions, but if it is in the data, no matter how much you revise the instructions, it is useless. This class covers criteria for determining where to fix something.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: Even if you tell your assistant to 'say something exactly', what happens if the exact value is nowhere to be found?

screens.outro: First, let me think about where I made improvements.

screens.title: Have you ever had the experience of constantly revising your guidelines to improve them?
screens.lead: If you first think about each question in your head and then select it, the instructor will organize your thoughts. You will not enter or submit an answer.

items.prompt: When you get an answer wrong, where do you go to first correct it?
items.answer: These are mostly guidelines. This is because the instructions are the easiest to open and the results of corrections are immediately visible. However, just because it's easy to fix doesn't mean you can assume the instructions are the cause.

items.prompt: Have you ever thought that there is room for correction outside the guidelines?
items.answer: Assistants are the result of guidance, knowledge, and connectors coming together. Guidelines determine behavior, knowledge provides references, and connectors bring in external information. Depending on which of these is lacking, where to fix it will depend.

screens.outro: Now let's distinguish between the three components that make up the assistant.

screens.title: The three components that make up an assistant
screens.lead: Select and expand each item to see instructions, knowledge, and the role the connector plays in your assistant.

items.title: Instructions: Decide how to act
items.body: Guidelines determine what your assistant should do, how it should respond, and what it should avoid. It applies to all conversations and drives tone, structure, and judgment. The GPT document advises using a ‘if something happens, do this’ structure for multi-step tasks, and to prefer positive, specific instructions such as ‘do this’ rather than a list of prohibitions. If you need to apply a definition or classification, ask them to include short examples of acceptable and unacceptable output.

items.title: Knowledge: Provides reference material when answering
items.body: Knowledge is a reference material that pulls information from uploaded files and allows you to answer. This includes documents, guides, handbooks and internal materials. The GPT document advises that knowledge be written in references rather than rules or actions, and that rules, tone, and workflow should be placed in instructions. Text-oriented files are recommended over files with complex layouts.

items.title: Connectors: Bring in external apps and data
items.body: Connectors connect external apps and data to your assistant. If the connector is broken or inaccessible, the response will not contain the information you need. For example, Claude's custom connector connects to a remote MCP server in Anthropic's cloud, so if the server is not accessible from the public internet, it may not connect.

items.title: Principle of repair order
items.body: The GPT documentation advises that problems can often be fixed more quickly if instructions are refined and examples are added before adding tools. This principle is a matter of guidance. If the symptom is a data issue, you should check the knowledge or connector first, not the instructions.

screens.outro: Now that we know the three components, let’s pair them with failure types.

screens.title: Mating from types to components
screens.lead: The table below lists the components to suspect first and specific correction methods for each type of failure. Read it line by line and check how the symptoms and fixes correspond.

data.caption: Types of failure and which components to suspect first
rows: Add necessary information to the knowledge file and replace old files with the latest ones. Check whether the connector is retrieving information.
Does the material actually contain information and is it in a format that the assistant can read?
Be specific about the output format and include an example or two.
Are the format instructions unambiguous and the examples are in the required format?
Have them cite the supporting documents first, and if they don't know, answer that they don't know.
Do you answer that you don’t know to questions that have no basis?
Replace old knowledge files with new files and check the connection status of external data.
Do the answers to the same questions change after posting new data?
data.notes: Knowledge is a reference, rules are guidelines. Putting the rules, tone, and workflow in instructions is the way to be guided, so move the rules in your knowledge file into instructions. Custom connectors also ensure that the connection itself may fail if the server is unreachable.

screens.outro: Now let's compare the risk of over-editing versus revising and checking again.

screens.title: Recheck after revision and risk of excessive revision
screens.lead: Switch between the two states to compare moderate correction and overcorrection.

states.label: decent modification
states.body: Fix only one place at a time. Then you can see which modifications worked. After making modifications, go back to the same set of questions and check whether the modified questions have improved and other questions have not worsened. We guide you through the order of checking and saving or updating GPT documents in Preview first. When improvements are made, keep a line-by-line note of what was changed and why it was improved.

states.label: overcorrection
states.body: If you keep adding rules in one place, you'll end up with conflicting rules. The longer the instructions, the more difficult it becomes to keep track of which rules affect which answers. If you fix several places at once, you won't know which fix worked. Excessive modification occurs when the error remains the same and only the instructions become more complicated. Before adding a rule, first check whether the rule is really targeting the cause. The same goes for the guidance that it is often quicker to refine the instructions and include examples before adding tools.

screens.outro: Now I will explain an example of a pricing error.

screens.title: Commentary: Pricing error is not a guideline but a data update issue
screens.lead: The instructor will first explain the process of categorizing the pricing error in question by type and determining where to fix it. Select the arrows and follow them step by step.

steps.title: Check for symptoms
steps.body: When asked about the price of the product, the answer was the previous price. The clue is that even though you changed the instructions ten times, you still got the same answer.

steps.title: Type classification
steps.body: The format is as required and there are no made up dates or figures. Because the data does not have the most up-to-date prices, the required information was not answered, so it is classified as missing. The old prices are not made up, they are taken from old data.

steps.title: Determine where to fix
steps.body: Omissions question knowledge or connectors. If the price list is uploaded to a knowledge file, check to see if that file is out of date. Even if you include 'speak clearly' in the guidelines, it is of no use if the exact values ​​are not in the data.

steps.title: Edit
steps.body: Replaces the price list in the knowledge file with the latest one. If you have a table with a complex layout, it will be easier to read if you organize it around the text. The instructions are not touched.

steps.title: Instructor's judgment
steps.body: The reason the effort to change the guidelines ten times was in vain was because the cause was not in the guidelines. Dividing symptoms into types and pairing the types with their components can help reduce the number of revisions and keep the instructions simple.

screens.outro: Once you've made your edits, you need to make sure they're properly improved.

screens.title: Explanation: Check again after editing
screens.lead: As you select each step, the instructor's commentary unfolds. This is the order to check after replacing the price tag.

items.prompt: 1. Repeat the set of pricing questions in the same order.
items.answer: You can compare by asking the same questions and in the same order as before editing. First, check that the price question is now answered with the latest values.

items.prompt: 2. Check whether other questions have become worse with the entire set
items.answer: We also ask questions other than price to see the impact. Changing the knowledge file may result in different answers to other questions, so don't just look at the modified question and end.

items.prompt: 3. What to do if you’re still wrong
items.answer: Check to see if there is a problem with not being able to read the knowledge file. Files with complex layouts may be difficult to import, and you must upload the file in Preview to check if it is used as intended.

items.prompt: 4. What do you do when you improve?
items.answer: Write down in one line what you fixed and why it was improved. You can quickly repeat the same judgment the next time you experience similar symptoms.

screens.outro: Lastly, let me summarize the main points.

screens.title: Fix the area that matches your symptoms
screens.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.

paragraphs: Assistants are the result of guidance, knowledge, and connectors coming together. The habit of correcting the instructions first when an error occurs is convenient, but it is useless if the data is the cause. The key is to divide failures into types and fix the components that fit those types.

Omissions question knowledge or connectors, formatting errors question instructions, and fabrications question the basis requirements. Then, after correcting one spot, we check again with the same set of questions. The habit of checking and recording effects, without adding too much, keeps the assistant simple and reliable.

callout.label: something to remember
callout.text: Divide symptoms into types, correct only one area at a time that matches the type, and check again with the same set.

checks.q: The assistant will reply with the past price. The format is correct and there is no made-up content. Where should I fix it first?
options: Added a sentence to the instructions to state the exact price
Replace the price list in the knowledge file with the latest one
checks.explain: This is an issue where the latest prices are missing from the data, so the knowledge file, which is a reference, needs to be updated.

wrong.0: Guidelines are where rules and behaviors are established, so the data itself does not solve outdated problems.
wrong.1: The tone of speech has nothing to do with the accuracy of the content.
wrong.3: The format is already correct, so adding an example will still leave the pricing error.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded.

checks.q: Put them in the right order to check after editing.
items: Repeat the set of pricing questions in the same order.
Also check the entire set to see if other questions have deteriorated.
If it is still incorrect, check whether the problem is not reading the knowledge file.
If there is improvement, record the reason in one line.
checks.explain: First, double-check your target questions and see the overall impact, then document any remaining issues to further narrow down their causes and improve them.
checks.intro: Put them in order, remembering the order you learned them. Results are not recorded.

glossary.def: Depending on the type of failure, it is a correspondence relationship that pairs which of the instructions, knowledge, and connectors to suspect first.
This is the process of repeating the same set of questions after making modifications and comparing the results.
A situation in which rules are continuously added in one place, resulting in conflicting rules and making it difficult to trace the cause.
This is an instruction that requires the response to cite supporting documents or to answer that they do not know if there is no evidence.

misconceptions.myth: If an error occurs, it is correct to correct the instructions first.
misconceptions.fact: You must choose a place that suits your symptoms. Errors caused by outdated data should be corrected from knowledge, not guidance.

misconceptions.myth: It is faster to fix several areas at once.
misconceptions.fact: You won't know which fix worked. Fix and check only one location at a time.

misconceptions.myth: If you write down the rules in a knowledge file, the assistant will follow them.
misconceptions.fact: Knowledge is the reference, and rules, tone, and workflow are placed in the guidance, which is how it is guided.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Fix the area that matches your symptoms.
Omissions question knowledge and connectors, format errors question instructions, and fabrications question the basis requirements.
Fix one spot and check again with the same set.
Avoid excessive modifications that just add rules.

closing.reflection: Where is my assistant's next point of revision: instructions, knowledge, or connectors?

title: Deciding what to improve: instructions, knowledge, or connectors
